events.continuity_hook: Carry the selected open-jaw flights, two viable Birmingham hotels, one-way rental totals and drop fees, Tuesday driving time from the Atlanta-area inspection, Wednesday hotel-to-restaurant timing, and the latest practical car-return time into the final purchase check.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the complete hotel-and-car combinations, confirm that Tuesday's drive and Wednesday's inspection fit the flight schedule, and select one arrangement without booking.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus has chosen the open-jaw itinerary into Atlanta and home from Birmingham because it preserves the full Wednesday inspection and avoids a return drive to Atlanta. He now needs a Tuesday-night hotel near the Birmingham restaurant and a one-way rental car; the lowest car quote has a large drop fee, while a slightly higher base rate produces a lower total and permits return shortly before the selected flight.

events.continuity_hook: Keep the completed flight, hotel, and rental confirmations together with final totals, cancellation terms, one-way fee, counter hours, Tuesday intercity route, and Wednesday inspection-to-airport schedule.
events.interaction_goal: Reprice all three components, verify dates and return logistics, and book the trip if the timing remains workable.
events.scenario_brief: The selected Birmingham hotel still has a one-night cancellable rate, and the lower-total rental company confirms that its one-way fee is included and that the Birmingham airport counter will be open at the planned return time. The open-jaw airfare has increased modestly, but the itinerary still costs less in work time than the Atlanta round trip.

events.continuity_hook: Carry the three-traveler flight totals, driving cost and duration estimate, usable time under each schedule, game and museum timing, and the three-night versus four-night lodging implications into the hotel search.
events.interaction_goal: Compare flying and driving door to door, determine whether the shorter flight schedule leaves enough time for both planned activities, and choose a transportation structure without purchasing.
events.scenario_brief: Marcus, his husband, and their son are considering a three-night weekend in Pittsburgh built around a Saturday afternoon baseball game and a Sunday museum visit. Driving from Chicago is cheaper but consumes much of Friday and Monday, while flying requires three fares plus local transportation; two flight schedules differ in whether the family needs a fourth hotel night.

events.continuity_hook: Retain two viable hotel candidates with room layouts for three, full taxes and fees, occupancy details, cancellation dates, transportation costs, and travel times to the ballpark, museum, and airport.
events.interaction_goal: Verify that each room accommodates all three travelers, compare complete stay and local transportation costs, and narrow the choice to one hotel without reserving it.
events.scenario_brief: The family has selected the three-night flight schedule and now needs lodging with practical access to the ballpark and museum. One downtown room lists two queens but adds substantial parking and destination charges, while a less expensive university-area room shows a king and sofa bed but does not clearly include a 12-year-old in the quoted occupancy; airport transit and rideshare costs also narrow the apparent price difference.

events.continuity_hook: Carry the final hotel comparison, confirmed sleeping arrangements, three-night totals, cancellation deadlines, local transportation estimate, and both current airfare tiers into the booking decision.
events.interaction_goal: Recalculate the complete weekend cost, choose between the two hotels based on location and ground travel, and book the selected flights and room.
events.scenario_brief: The university-area property confirms that the sofa bed can be prepared for the son and that three-person occupancy is included, but its cancellable rate has risen. The downtown two-queen room remains available and is now close in total price after estimated rideshares are added; the preferred outbound flight has also moved to a higher fare tier that includes earlier seat selection.

events.continuity_hook: Keep the booked hotel and outbound flight together with the altered return time, earlier-flight price difference, seat availability for three, luggage-hold confirmation, airport travel estimates, and any resulting fare credit or payment.
events.interaction_goal: Compare accepting the later return with moving to the earlier flight, account for luggage and airport timing, and update the reservation only if the earlier option materially improves the day.
events.scenario_brief: The airline has moved the family's Monday return flight nearly three hours later, creating a long gap after hotel checkout but not affecting the Saturday game or Sunday museum plan. An earlier same-day flight is available with a fare difference, and the booked hotel can hold luggage after checkout; changing airports would require new ground transportation and split the family across seat rows.
